# Ryan J Hamby

> Senior Software Engineer on an inference data plane at an AI company (previously AWS, payments and IoT). Works on AI compute: serving, GPU telemetry, and low-latency systems in Rust, C++ and Go. Based in New York.

Focus: inference serving, GPU performance, distributed systems, exactly-once payment and metering systems, coding-agent guardrails.

Get in touch about inference performance, benchmarking methodology, or payments correctness (email below).

Public claims here are backed by repos and dated history. Where a figure is not from a captured run, the page says so.

## Proof

- [Projects](https://ryanjhamby.dev/projects/): index with status and dates for each project
- [vllm-project/vllm#48420](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/48420): merged fix, Qwen3-Omni multimodal processing crash
- [firecracker#6032](https://github.com/firecracker-microvm/firecracker/pull/6032): merged fix, VMM panic on ACPI device restore
- [FlowState](https://github.com/RyanJHamby/FlowState): Rust temporal join engine
- [autopilot-kit](https://github.com/RyanJHamby/autopilot-kit): SHA-pinned workflows and stdlib scripts that gate coding agents working across repos
- [Order Book Engine](https://github.com/RyanJHamby/order-book-engine): C++20 matching engine; P50 0.21 us, P99.9 3.1-3.2 us, 1.4-1.8M orders/sec on an isolated EC2 c6i.large core (3 runs)
- [GPU Flight Recorder](https://github.com/RyanJHamby/distributed-gpu-training-flight-recorder): implemented and validated in simulation only; no real-hardware results yet
